item.title: Dutch swimming water increasingly polluted, researchers find
item.description:
Dutch swimming water increasingly polluted, researchers find

September 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Swimming water in the Netherlands is still often polluted with chemicals and bacteria, according to new research by an environmental group and The Netherlands Institute for Ecology.

The researchers investigated the water quality from 205 official swimming locations and 57 other popular urban swimming spots

They were looking for 122 pollutants and found excess quantities of 35 substances in ponds, rivers and lakes around the country.

According the report, the number of locations with pollution rising. In particular incidents of blue-green algae have gone up in the past five years.

Water quality testing in the Netherlands focuses primarily on contaminants that cause acute health risks like blue-green algae and E. coli, and doesn’t include industrial substances and pesticides.

The group is calling for for stricter licensing of waste water disposal and increased monitoring of bathing waters.

item.title: Little help for girls in NL caught up in crime: study
item.description:
Little help for girls in NL caught up in crime: study

September 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

There is very little help for girls and young women who get caught up in the Dutch criminal justice system, a new government-backed study has found. The findings show the majority of treatment options are aimed at boys, who have different needs and problems.

The study is by the justice ministry’s research centre WODC and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. They looked at 22 international treatment methods for young female criminal offenders.

Only one such method is studied, used and seen as promising for girls in the Netherlands: a treatment that helps them manage aggression. For most other kinds of help, it is simply not known whether they do any good.

Different problems
Most programmes are built around boys, who make up the majority of young offenders. But girls and young women usually end up in the system for different reasons.

Their behaviour more often traces back to issues such as anxiety, trouble with their parents, or sexual abuse. Boys are more likely to struggle with aggression, poor self-control, or falling in with the wrong crowd.

Because of that, help designed for boys does not always help girls – especially the lighter support given at home or through youth care.

Divided opinions
Not all experts and researchers agree this is a problem. Some say programmes are always tailored to the individual anyway, so they work for boys and girls alike. Others want clearer guidance for working with girls.

Girls and young women are behind only a small share of recorded crime, usually less serious, such as theft.

Among the youngest, under 16, there has been a slight rise in violent offences. Why is not clear. It follows a wider rise in teen crime recorded last year.

item.title: Multiple weapons found in search around Overasselt
item.description:
Multiple weapons found in search around Overasselt

September 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police found multiple weapons during a search of several locations in and around the Gelderland town at the centre of a drugs dispute, where dozens of armed men were seen roaming the streets this week, leaving one man dead and two police officers injured.

Investigators, looking into violence in Overasselt, found a cache of weapons on Wednesday in the nearby town of Wijchen following a tip from a resident.

An order for residents to stay inside their homes was lifted on Wednesday.

Police responded to call about a robbery at a home in the early hours of Tuesday morning. A 51-year old security guard was killed and two officers were injured in the ensuing violence.

Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf later posted security camera videos showing a group of at least 30 masked men – some carrying what appear to be automatic rifles – outside a property.

Police have arrested 34 people in connection with the incident and say the attack was the result of a “long-running conflict.”

The property has a long history of drug-related incidents. A drug lab was found there after a fire in 2019, and the same address was shot at with an AK-47 last year.

According to broadcaster NOS, police were investigating a video that surfaced on social media threatening one of the residents, accusing Jan G. Jr – a resident of the property – of stealing a shipment of cocaine.

Dutch media have connected Jan G. Jr to drugs baron Jos “Bolle Jos” Leijdekkers, who is wanted in the Netherlands and Belgium for narcotics trafficking and other offences.

He is currently thought to be in West Africa and suspected of being behind the biggest shipment of cocaine ever intercepted, which was found in Spain earlier this year.

item.title: Fourth Dutch case of West Nile fever this year confirmed
item.description:
Fourth Dutch case of West Nile fever this year confirmed

September 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A woman from Amstelveen has contracted a rare form of meningitis from with the West Nile virus, the local health board has confirmed.

The 39-year-old woman is the fourth person known to have been infected with the virus in the Netherlands this year but the first to develop meningitis, which occurs in around 1% of cases.

West Nile virus is transmitted by mosquitos, but previously was caught by people who travelled abroad.

The public health agency RIVM said his year’s cluster of cases in humans, horses and birds show the diseased is now established in the Netherlands.

A week ago the RIVM confirmed that a man had died in hospital in Utrecht from West Nile fever after being infected locally. A woman in Drenthe died from the same illness, but she caught the virus while travelling.

The RIVM will publish an update on the current cases later this week. The agency stressed that the risk of serious illness or death is very low, with 80% of people reporting no symptoms at all.

Another 19% experience mild symptoms such as fever, headache, stomach ache and diarrhoea, as well as occasional skin rashes and swollen lymph nodes.

item.title: Police investigate threat video linked to Overasselt attack
item.description:
Police investigate threat video linked to Overasselt attack

September 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A video has surfaced on social media of masked men threatening an attack on Jan G. Jr, a resident of the property that was assaulted by armed men in Overasselt, Gelderland on Tuesday morning.

The video, which police have said they are investigating but has not yet been verified, shows four men in balaclavas, three holding automatic weapons. One reads out a statement in a heavy Spanish accent, accusing Jan G. Jr of stealing 1,283 kilograms of cocaine and two transport trucks.

“You have 12 hours to give the goods back and contact your ‘Belgian friend’”, the man reads, “after that we don’t want our goods anymore, but we promise we are going to kill everyone you love.”

The veracity of the video is still being analysed but it did not surface online before today, according to broadcaster NOS.

The video matches what Telegraaf and Het Parool have reported: that the shooting, in which more than 30 armed men killed a man and fired on police, was a gangland score settling.

Speculation has also been made that the attack was linked to drugs baron Jos “Bolle Jos” Leijdekkers, who is wanted in both the Netherlands and Belgium for narcotics trafficking and other offences, and is suspected to be behind a drugs bust in Spain this year – the largest single shipment capture ever recorded.

Leijdekkers’ lawyers have released a statement denying he had any involvement in the incident, telling news service ANP he “firmly distances himself from the unfounded accusations being repeatedly made against him.”

Many residents in Overasselt want the family associated with Jan G. Jr gone. They told NOS they had lived through repeated trouble at the property and hoped the council would step in, with one saying they wanted the family out for good so people no longer had to live in fear. Most would only speak anonymously, saying they feared repercussions.

item.title: Cabinet set to postpone asset tax reform again to 2029
item.description:
Cabinet set to postpone asset tax reform again to 2029

September 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Plans to reform the Netherlands’ asset tax system are likely to be delayed for another year as a result of the draft budget deal agreed at the weekend.

The cabinet had hoped to bring in a new mechanism for taxing assets, savings and investments to replace the fictional “box 3” interest rate by 2028.

But junior finance minister Eelco Eerenberg now looks set to withdraw the bill from the Senate to address criticism of the replacement system from opposition parties. If the vote is postponed it is unlikely that the bill can become law before 2029.

The previous system was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2021, when it ruled that taxing unrealised assets on a flat rate, based on the notional average annual return, violated the European Convention on Human Rights.

The rate was initially charged on all wealth above a basic threshold, regardless of whether they were invested in deposit return savings or high-risk investment vehicles with potentially much higher returns.

It also did not take into account overall market performance, so investors still paid tax on their assets even when they made a loss.

Capital gains

The new system planned to tax actual returns by making them submit details of all their savings and investments with their annual income tax return, which would add to the administrative burden.

But right-wing opposition parties want the government to introduce a capital gains tax, which investors pay on the money they make on their assets when they sell them.

In the meantime the cabinet has introduced an interim box 3 system with different fictional rates for deposit savings, investments and debts, which change every year to reflect market performance.

However, savers can claim a refund if they can show their actual returns were lower than the fictional amount, while not being required to pay more tax for higher returns.

The “best of both options” approach is estimated to cost the Dutch treasury some €2 billion a year.

item.title: Dutch central bank moves gold out of US and Canada
item.description:
Dutch central bank moves gold out of US and Canada

September 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch central bank (DNB) has moved about 86 tonnes of gold out of the United States and Canada to London, saying the reserves can be sold faster there in a crisis.

DNB said the transfer took place between March and August this year, and amounts to more than a quarter of the roughly 313 tonnes it had held in New York and Ottawa combined.

London is the world’s main trading centre for physical gold, and the bank said metal stored there is quicker to deploy than gold held in the US or Canada. It framed the move as part of wider work on “crisis readiness” amid growing geopolitical tension.

Most of the gold came out of the underground vault in Manhattan. Around 59 tonnes was sold in New York and bought back in London, which avoided melting down the bars and risking a loss of quality. A further 27 tonnes was physically shipped from the US and Canada to the DNB vault in Zeist, with the same quantity moved on from Zeist to London.

The share of Dutch gold held in New York has fallen from 31.3% to 18.5%, and Canada’s from 19.7% to 18.5%. London now holds the largest single share at 32.1%, up from 18.1%, while 30.8% remains in the Netherlands.

“We assume that we will never need to deploy the gold, but it is nevertheless necessary to strengthen our resilience and preparedness,” DNB president Olaf Sleijpen said.

DNB has repeatedly warned about Dutch reliance on the US since Donald Trump returned to the White House, though it has said it is not worried the US would seize the reserves. The Netherlands held 612.4 tonnes of gold, worth €72.2 billion, at the end of 2025.

item.title: Ex-ministers and diplomats urge tougher action against Israel
item.description:
Ex-ministers and diplomats urge tougher action against Israel

September 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

More than 230 former Dutch ministers, ambassadors, diplomats and civil servants have called on the cabinet to take far tougher measures against Israel, including a full arms embargo and the suspension of the European Union’s trade agreement with the country.

The appeal comes as the Netherlands prepares to enforce its ban on settlement goods on September 22.

That measure led Israel to expel two Dutch officials from the US-backed Gaza ceasefire centre last week. The signatories say steps of this kind fall far short of what the situation demands.

Those who signed include former Amsterdam mayor Job Cohen, former foreign minister Jozias van Aartsen, former Rotterdam mayor Ahmed Aboutaleb, former development minister Jan Pronk and former defence minister Joris Voorhoeve.

According to NRC, the signatories held office for the Labour party (PvdA), the Christian Democrats (CDA) and the right-wing liberal VVD.

In the letter, the group calls for a complete arms embargo, the suspension of the EU-Israel trade agreement, and an investigation into possible involvement in international crimes by Dutch nationals and by Israelis living in the Netherlands who have served in the Israeli army.

The Netherlands already restricts some military exports to Israel. The signatories want measures that, in their words, match the scale of the violations taking place.

One of the signatories, former diplomat Angélique Eijpe, who left the foreign ministry over its stance on Gaza, said government policy had barely shifted. “We had cautiously hoped the Jetten cabinet would choose a different course,” she told broadcaster NOS in Dutch. “We see steps that mainly have a symbolic impact but do not bring about a change in behaviour.”

It is not the first such appeal – some of the same figures called for international intervention in Gaza a year ago, following a similar call earlier in 2025.

Eijpe said the group did not expect the letter to change policy overnight. “But the situation is so serious that we consider it necessary to keep putting it on the radar,” she told NOS.

item.title: Drummer Alex van Halen given knighthood in home city of Nijmegen
item.description:
Drummer Alex van Halen given knighthood in home city of Nijmegen

September 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Alex van Halen, one of two Dutch brothers who founded the US rock band Van Halen, has been given one of the Netherlands’ highest civil honours.

The 73-year-old drummer was made a knight in the Order of the Netherlands Lion after being nominated by his home city of Nijmegen.

The city said it had recognised Van Halen for his distinctive drumming style, calling it “powerful, dynamic and precise.”

Van Halen, who flew from the United States to receive the honour at a ceremony in from the mayor of Nijmegen, Hubert Bruls, said he was “very grateful”. He also signed the book of the city.

“I think institutions like this are important in people’s lives because it adds a dignity and a gravity to what we do,” he said.

“Whether it’s actually deserved or not, that’s another question. But we can live up to it.”

Nijmegen to Pasadena

Alex and his younger brother Eddie started the band in 1970, eight years after the family moved from Nijmegen to Pasadena in the United States.

Their best-known hits were Jump and Runnin with the Devil, distinguished by Eddie van Halen’s virtuoso performances on guitar.

Originally Eddie wanted to be a drummer while Alex played guitar, but the brothers swapped roles by the time they formed their first band in school, The Broken Combs. They were also classically trained pianists.

In 2019 part of the Hunnerpark was temporarily renamed Van Halenplein and a mural was painted in honour of Eddie van Halen.

The band Van Halen stayed together until Eddie’s death in 2020 at the age of 65.

item.title: Dutch woman living in Nepal found alive after surviving floods
item.description:
Dutch woman living in Nepal found alive after surviving floods

September 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch foreign office has made contact with a woman living in Nepal who had been reported missing in the wake of last week’s devastating floods, which have killed more than 1,100 people.

Foreign affairs minister Tom Berendsen said there had been “good news” as he spoke to reporters during a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Ireland.

The woman is one of three Dutch nationals who were known to be in Nepal when a glacier in the Himalaya region collapsed last Wednesday, causing water and mud to surge down the Bhote Koshi river and wipe out villages in the Rawusa border region with Tibet.

She was in the Himalaya region when the disaster struck, but has reached the Nepalese capital Kathmandu, where she contacted the foreign ministry.

A spokesman said the government was still “very concerned about the fate of the two other Dutch nationals”, 29-year-old Christiaan Berghuis from Nijkerk and 51-year-old Maaike Moolhuijsen from Haarlem.

They were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, a sacred Tibetan mountain, when the floods hit. The group of 80 pilgrims were believed to be in an immigration office that was in the path of the floodwaters.
